claim: An on-demand stream scales automatically when write throughput reaches a new peak. Write throttling can occur if traffic increases to more than double the previous peak within a 15-minute duration, and you need to retry the throttled requests.
question: When can an on-demand Kinesis data stream throttle writes, and what should the producer do?

values.display: more than double the previous peak
retry these throttled requests

evidence.quote: As your data stream’s write throughput reaches a new peak, Kinesis Data Streams scales the data stream’s capacity automatically. For example, if your data stream has a write throughput that varies between 10 MB/s and 40 MB/s, then Kinesis Data Streams ensures that you can easily burst to double your previous peak throughput, or 80 MB/s. If the same data stream sustains a new peak throughput of 50 MB/s, Kinesis Data Streams ensures that there is enough capacity to ingest 100 MB/s of write throughput. However, write throttling can occur if your traffic increases to more than double the previous peak within a 15-minute duration. You need to retry these throttled requests.

claim: In on-demand mode the data stream automatically adapts to uneven data distribution unless a single partition key exceeds a shard's 1 MB/s throughput and 1000 records per second limits.

1000 records per second

qualifiers.condition: a single partition key that drives more traffic than one shard can take

evidence.quote: You may experience read and write exceptions if you are using a partition key that leads to uneven data distribution, and the records assigned to a particular shard exceed its limits. With on-demand mode, the data stream automatically adapts to handle uneven data distribution patterns unless a single partition key exceeds a shard’s 1 MB/s throughput and 1000 records per second limits.

claim: In on-demand mode Kinesis Data Streams splits shards evenly when traffic increases but does not detect and isolate hash keys that drive a higher share of traffic to one shard. For highly uneven partition keys AWS recommends provisioned mode, which supports granular shard splits.
question: What mode should you use when partition keys are highly uneven and on-demand mode keeps returning write exceptions?

values.display: does not detect and isolate hash keys
provisioned capacity mode that supports granular shard splits

evidence.quote: In the on-demand mode, Kinesis Data Streams splits the shards evenly when it detects an increase in traffic. However, it does not detect and isolate hash keys that are driving a higher portion of incoming traffic to a particular shard. If you are using highly uneven partition keys you may continue to receive write exceptions. For such use cases, we recommend that you use the provisioned capacity mode that supports granular shard splits.

claim: In provisioned mode, if a partition key leads to uneven data distribution and a shard exceeds its limits, identify those shards and split them manually. If the stream is not configured for peak throughput, you must scale it manually.
question: How do you fix a hot shard in a provisioned-mode Kinesis data stream?

values.display: identify such shards and manually split them
manually scale your data stream

evidence.quote: You may also experience read and write exceptions if you're using a partition key that leads to uneven data distribution and the records assigned to a shard exceed its limits. To resolve this issue in the provisioned mode, identify such shards and manually split them to better accommodate your traffic.

while there is a Kinesis Data Streams producer or consumer application

evidence.quote: With provisioned mode, after you create the data stream, you can dynamically scale your shard capacity up or down using the AWS Management Console or the [UpdateShardCount](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateShardCount.html) API. You can make updates while there is a Kinesis Data Streams producer or consumer application writing to or reading data from the stream.

claim: Switching a data stream between on-demand and provisioned mode does not disrupt applications: you can keep writing to and reading from the stream. The stream status is Updating until it returns to Active.
question: Does switching a Kinesis data stream between capacity modes interrupt producers and consumers?

values.display: doesn't cause any disruptions to your applications
status of the stream is set to Updating

evidence.quote: Switching between modes doesn't cause any disruptions to your applications that use this data stream. You can continue writing to and reading from this data stream. As you're switching between modes, either from on-demand to provisioned or from provisioned to on-demand, the status of the stream is set to *Updating*.

claim: When you switch from provisioned to on-demand mode, the stream keeps its shard count at first and Kinesis Data Streams then scales it with your write throughput. When you switch from on-demand to provisioned, the stream also keeps its shard count, and you become responsible for adjusting it.
question: What happens to the shard count when you switch a stream between provisioned and on-demand mode?

values.display: initially retains whatever shard count it had
you're responsible for monitoring and adjusting the shard count

evidence.quote: When you switch from provisioned to on-demand capacity mode, your data stream initially retains whatever shard count it had before the transition, and from this point on, Kinesis Data Streams monitors your data traffic and scales the shard count of this on-demand data stream depending on your write throughput. When you switch from on-demand to provisioned mode, your data stream also initially retains whatever shard count it had before the transition, but from this point on, you're responsible for monitoring and adjusting the shard count of this data stream to properly accomodate your write throughput.

claim: In any capacity mode you can write with the PutRecord and PutRecords APIs. All three modes support default consumers that use GetRecords and enhanced fan-out consumers that use SubscribeToShard.

GetRecords API and Enhanced Fan-Out (EFO) consumers

evidence.quote: You can use Kinesis Data Streams `PutRecord` and `PutRecords` APIs to write data into your data streams in any mode. To retrieve data, all three modes support default consumers that use the `GetRecords` API and Enhanced Fan-Out (EFO) consumers that use the `SubscribeToShard` API.

claim: Splitting shards increases the capacity and the cost of a stream, and merging shards reduces its cost and capacity. You can use metrics to find hot or cold shards, split hot shards and merge cold shards.
question: What do shard splits and merges change in a provisioned Kinesis data stream?

values.display: split shards to increase the capacity (and cost)
merge shards to reduce the cost (and capacity)

evidence.quote: The purpose of resharding in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is to enable your stream to adapt to changes in the rate of data flow. You split shards to increase the capacity (and cost) of your stream. You merge shards to reduce the cost (and capacity) of your stream.
